about: Stories the answer keys name that are two reports of one event or one study, which production's duplicate detection would have merged: the linking replays feed each group as one story, its keep (ADR-0076; .context/model-eval.md, "Deduplicated inputs"). The keep is the earliest published, the earliest crawled breaking a tie. Only groups rated medium or better; the keys check holds every group to the keys (duplicates.ts).

groups.why: The first US and Israeli strikes on Iran of 28 February and Iran's missiles fired back, reported the next day by three outlets.
Iran's strikes across the Gulf on energy sites and US bases in the war's first days, reported a day apart.
Israel's strikes on Beirut of 12 March after Hezbollah's rockets, with the same toll and 800,000 displaced.
Trump's order of 12 April for a US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
The WMO's early-June El Niño update (80 to 90% likely, more heat, droughts and floods), from the UN's own news and from Rappler.
The US-Iran deal announced on 15 June to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with its signing set in Switzerland.
Guterres's and the WMO's warning of 31 July that the strengthening El Niño will drive heat, floods and droughts.
The WFP's analysis of 5 August that El Niño could push about 50 million more people into acute hunger.
The Science study of Galapagos coral records linking more variable El Niño cycles to fossil-fuel warming.
The phased deal under discussion in late September: Iran reopens the strait, the US lifts its blockade and frees assets.
The UN high-level meeting on pandemic prevention of 25 September, from WHO's news item and from Tedros's remarks there.
The signs in late October that the US, with Israel, is preparing renewed strikes on Iran.
WHO clearing two Bundibugyo vaccine candidates (Oxford's and Moderna's) for the trial in DR Congo.
